raw_response:
I have farmed this land a long time, so I will start from what I did before and only adjust a little. My place is 8 mu, not very big, and some people in my family work outside, so I cannot make the work too scattered. Cotton is still my main crop because I know how to manage it and I have well water, so I am not too afraid if spring is dry. I will keep more land in cotton, then leave some for maize and a small piece for mungbean. Maize gives steady grain for the house and sale, and mungbean does not need as much fertilizer, so it helps me save some money on one piece of land. I learned from years in the field and from hearing what the seed and fertilizer sellers say, but I still look first at what worked nearby. Last year if I cut fertilizer too much, the crop looked weak, so this year I will not be stingy. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. On cotton I will use a bit heavier fertilizer and more sprays, because that crop is fussy. On maize I will use hybrid seed because it usually yields better. On mungbean I will keep inputs lower, since it is a smaller crop and too much spending on it does not pay. I will use rotary tillage on all three because it saves labor compared with deep ploughing every piece, and with my well I will water the key times, not too many times, just enough to hold the yield.
